products.title: ST x Mogshade Headcover, Driver
products.body_html:
We've collaborated with Mogshade to make our SLICE TOWN guy into a headcover for your most precious woods.

  • Fits all 400-460CC Drivers.
  • Approx. 27cm tall with 16cm of opening width.
  • Yellow churra wool
  • Pink interior from deadstock polyester

Mathces with our fairway headcover.

Specifications

  • Outer Shell: 100% churra wool
  • Linings: 100% deadstock polyester
  • Patchwork art: 100% burel wool
  • Brand Label: 100% recycled polyester
  • Composition Label: 100% cotton
  • Elastic: 50% rubber, 50% polyester
  • Thread: 100% polyester

Origins

Every material has an origin, and this one starts in the Guarda mountains. There, the Manta Lobeira is still made from churra wool, woven by hand on a loom that has been in use for three centuries. The only certified team still making the true Cobertor de Papa keeps the tradition alive, a craft molded by the highlands and the lives lived among them. Its density, toughness, and texture are not design choices but answers to hard conditions: thin air, bitter cold, and constant exposure. Made to be used, it is inseparable from the land and culture behind it. Long before it was part of golf, it was part of the mountains.

For this collaboration, we created a headcover that brings the heft, tactility, and heritage of the original textile into a different world.

  • Thread: 100% polyester

Origins

Before it became anything else, it began high in the mountains of Guarda. The Manta Lobeira is still woven from churra wool on a manual loom that is 300 years old. Today the craft lives on in the hands of the last certified team producing the authentic Cobertor de Papa, a textile tradition shaped by the highlands and by the people who lived in them. The fabric's density, resilience, and texture come straight from the conditions that demanded it: altitude, cold, exposure, and daily use. Its character cannot be separated from the landscape and culture that formed it. Before it belonged to golf, it belonged to the mountains.

For this collaboration, we designed a headcover that carries the weight, feel, and memory of the original material into a new setting.

products.title: Depeche Golf Issue #5
products.body_html:
Issue #5 of the independent golf magazine, Depeche Golf, with 'Home' as its main theme.

SLICE TOWN is part of this issue's game changers section.

Product Description

Here's what Depeche has to say about the magazine:

The issue looks into places and ideas related to the concepts behind the word HOME. We headed up to St Andrews where the historic home of golf is constantly changing; we made the road our home for a wild summer of golf in Ireland and visited the Engadine Golf Club in St Moritz, a mountain town widely seen as the Swiss home of golf. We portrayed the guys from our home course down the road and went on a quest for the vanishing greens of Singapore. We were guests at the world’s oldest building used as a clubhouse and visited an artist in New Zealand who built an unplayable golf course through his hometown Christchurch. We dove into the philosophy of home and considered the nature of the flag. We went looking for Missing Links in the far-east, had a lesson with the Old Pro and learnt there is finally a doctor on the course, while our Photographer in Residence brought us views of other people’s homes and courses.

Contents

HOME IMPROVEMENTS

Mark Alexander

OUR OWN HIDDEN REALM

Matt Chominski + Barry Bradshaw

HOME ON THE ROAD
